clue.text: A strip needs dancing — these people are taking steps

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and shift position, so this phrase is rearranged

explanation.surface: A striptease routine calls for dancing, it seems, with people stepping around the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dancing' looks like part of the act but signals that the letters of A STRIP NEEDS are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Walkers on foot are, quite literally, people taking steps along the street.

clue.text: The old man not in his own place minding offspring?

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father, the old man
a tenant renting lives in a home they do not own

explanation.surface: A father living away from his own home while looking after the kids.
explanation.definitionFit: Raising children means looking after them, minding the young.

clue.text: Outstanding romantic event — or time for the result?

parts.note: due means outstanding, as a debt still to be paid
a date is a romantic outing

explanation.surface: A wonderful romantic evening, or the moment the consequences arrive.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Outstanding' wants to mean excellent; it means owed. 'the result' hints at a baby following romance.
explanation.definitionFit: An expected birth or deadline falls on this day, when the outcome arrives.

clue.text: Covert aide for people on boards?

definitions.text: Covert aide for people on boards?

parts.words: Covert aide for people on boards?
parts.note: the boards are the theatre stage, and the unseen helper moves scenery for the actors

explanation.surface: A secret assistant serving company directors who sit on boards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boards' suggests a boardroom; 'the boards' is the stage, where actors tread.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre crew member works unseen behind the scenes, helping the performers.

clue.text: Machine found in origin around Belgium

indicators.note: around means the first piece surrounds the second

parts.note: a root is an origin or source
B is the international vehicle code for Belgium

explanation.surface: A machine discovered to have originated in Belgium.
explanation.definitionFit: An automaton is a programmable machine that carries out tasks by itself.

clue.text: Charles de Gaulle maybe left following broadcast

indicators.note: following means this piece comes after the other one

parts.note: to air something is to broadcast it
port is the left side of a ship

explanation.surface: General de Gaulle perhaps departed after making a broadcast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Charles de Gaulle' suggests the French leader; it is also the main Paris air hub, an example signalled by 'maybe'.
explanation.definitionFit: Paris-Charles de Gaulle is an example of a major international aviation hub.

clue.text: Argument prepared with books circulating

parts.note: set means ready or prepared

indicators.note: circulating means turning round, so the piece is written backwards

parts.note: OT is the Old Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: A dispute arises once the books are ready and circulating.
explanation.walkthrough: 'circulating' turns OT to TO.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief fight or squabble is a quarrel, an argument.

clue.text: Prickly shrub cutting taken from sapling or seedling

indicators.note: a cutting is a piece snipped from a plant, so a run of letters is taken out of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A gardener takes a cutting of a spiny bush from young plants.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cutting taken from' reads as horticulture but points to letters running across saplinG OR SEedling.
explanation.definitionFit: Also called furze or whin, it is a spiny yellow-flowered heathland bush.

clue.text: A date Kevin fixed after end of spring to make mutual concessions

indicators.note: after means the rearranged letters follow the single letter
end of picks the final letter of the word that follows
fixed here means repaired or rearranged, so the letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: A date Kevin arranged for the end of spring, with both sides compromising.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fixed' rearranges A DATE KEVIN to IVEANDTAKE, placed after G.
explanation.definitionFit: Compromise in which each side yields something is an idiom for mutual concession.

clue.text: Where elders may be seen between services?

definitions.text: Where elders may be seen between services?

parts.words: Where elders may be seen between services?
parts.note: church elders might be met between services, but elders here are elder trees, grown in a collection of trees

explanation.surface: Church elders mingling somewhere in the gap between Sunday services.
explanation.walkthrough: 'elders' wants to mean senior churchgoers; it is the elder tree, found in a botanical tree garden.
explanation.definitionFit: A botanical garden devoted to trees would show elder trees among its specimens.

clue.text: Team disseminated science — and type of philosophy

indicators.note: disseminated means scattered widely, so these letters are spread out in a new order

parts.note: physics is a branch of science

explanation.surface: A team spread their scientific findings, along with some philosophy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'disseminated' turns TEAM into META.
explanation.definitionFit: This branch of philosophy deals with the nature of being and reality.

clue.text: Classic label retained by crime writer

indicators.note: retained by means one piece is held inside another

parts.note: Barbara Vine was the pen name used by crime novelist Ruth Rendell
a tag is a label attached to something

explanation.surface: A mystery author keeps hold of a classic label, perhaps a publisher's imprint.
explanation.walkthrough: Barbara Vine was the pseudonym of crime novelist Ruth Rendell.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe something of lasting high quality from a notable earlier period, like a fine car or wine.

clue.text: Thoughtlessly produce rubbish defended by solicitor

indicators.note: defended by means the first piece is shielded on both sides by the second

parts.note: a tout is one who solicits custom, so a solicitor in the literal sense
rot means nonsense or rubbish

explanation.surface: A lawyer defends a client by churning out nonsense without thinking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'solicitor' suggests a lawyer but is TOUT, someone touting or soliciting business.
explanation.definitionFit: To trot out an excuse is to repeat it mechanically, without fresh thought.

clue.text: Private comment in a group in field?

parts.note: a side is a team taking the field in a sport

explanation.surface: A quiet remark made among a group of players on the pitch.
explanation.definitionFit: In theatre, a remark spoken so only the audience hears it is a private comment to them.

clue.text: A fight's cool to make a comeback in the main

definitions.text: make a comeback in the main

parts.note: a bout is a fight, and the 's is read as a letter S
hip means fashionable or cool

explanation.surface: A boxer's fight is cool enough to stage a comeback in the main event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the main' is the open sea, an old poetic term.
explanation.definitionFit: The sailing command orders a vessel to turn round onto the other tack, coming back across the sea.

clue.text: Venture too far having completed stretch of river

parts.note: over means finished or completed
a reach is a straight stretch of a river

explanation.surface: Someone goes too far after finishing a stretch along a river.
explanation.definitionFit: To overstretch oneself is to attempt more than one can manage.

clue.text: Unfriendliness of publican I fired before start of year

parts.note: a publican hosts guests at a pub, so is a host
lit means set alight, fired

indicators.note: start of picks the first letter of the word that follows

explanation.surface: A publican's unfriendly attitude: I was sacked before the year began.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fired' suggests sacking; it means set alight.
explanation.definitionFit: Hostile behaviour means open antagonism or enmity.

clue.text: Walk in the park to accommodate doctor, and a form of swimming

indicators.note: to accommodate means the outer word takes the other pieces inside it

parts.note: a doddle, like a walk in the park, is something very easy
GP stands for general practitioner, a family doctor

explanation.surface: A stroll in the park makes room for a doctor, alongside some swimming.
explanation.walkthrough: DODDLE is British slang for an easy task; it takes in GP and A.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a simple paddling stroke imitating how a dog swims.

clue.text: Stuffy East-ender's thin on top

indicators.note: a Cockney from London's East End traditionally drops the initial aitch

parts.note: being bald, thin on top, is to be hairless

explanation.surface: A stuffy Londoner from the East End is going bald.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockneys from London's East End are said to drop their aitches.
explanation.definitionFit: A room lacking fresh air or ventilation feels close and stuffy.

clue.text: Retired Irish broadcaster liable to mishap

indicators.note: retired means drawn back, so the short piece is written backwards

parts.note: Sky is a British satellite television broadcaster

explanation.surface: A retired Irish broadcaster is prone to blunders on air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Retired' looks like a career note about the broadcaster but turns the Irish abbreviation round; Sky is the British satellite TV company.
explanation.definitionFit: Something hazardous carries a real chance of accident or loss.

clue.text: Gentleman served up German dish

indicators.note: served up in a down clue means written upwards, reversed

parts.note: sir is a polite title for a gentleman
Otto is a typical German man's name

explanation.surface: A gentleman serves a German dish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'served up' in a down clue turns SIR to RIS.
explanation.definitionFit: An Italian rice preparation cooked slowly in stock is a well-known dish.

clue.text: Drove round bend in green convertible in promotion

indicators.note: in means one piece goes inside another

parts.note: an ad is an advertisement or promotion

indicators.note: convertible letters can be changed into another form, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone drove a green convertible round a bend while advertising it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drove round bend' looks like motoring but is the idiom for infuriated; 'convertible' is not the car but the signal that the colour's letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To drive someone round the bend is the idiom for infuriating them.

clue.text: Prepare man at union

definitions.meaning: to get ready or train someone for a role
a bridegroom is the man getting married at the wedding

explanation.surface: Getting a man ready for a meeting of the trade union.
explanation.definitionFit: Grooming means preparing, and the bridegroom is the husband at a wedding.

clue.text: Condescend to make mention of Scandinavian

indicators.note: make mention of means to say out loud, so a word of the same sound is entered

parts.note: a Dane is a Scandinavian from Denmark

explanation.surface: Lowering oneself to speak of a Scandinavian.
explanation.definitionFit: To stoop to do something one thinks beneath one's dignity is to condescend.

clue.text: Composer somewhat cross in interview

indicators.note: somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A composer who is a little irritated during an interview.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian who wrote The Barber of Seville, a famous composer.

clue.text: Mysterious objects I store haphazardly carried by European roughly

indicators.note: carried by means held between, so the jumbled letters sit inside the other pieces

parts.note: CA, short for circa, means roughly

indicators.note: haphazardly means at random, so these letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: Someone keeps curious items haphazardly, carried by a European, more or less.
explanation.walkthrough: 'roughly' gives CA from circa, the Latin for approximately; the shuffled letters sit between the European abbreviation and it.
explanation.definitionFit: Esoteric means understood only by a few initiates, so such items are obscure curiosities.

clue.text: It could be one's reaction to flip stories heard

definitions.text: It could be one's reaction to flip

indicators.note: heard means the word is spoken, so a word with the same sound is entered

parts.note: tales are stories

explanation.surface: Someone flips out after hearing stories, and this is how they react.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flip' suggests losing one's temper; it is a coin toss, where the call might be 'tails'.
explanation.definitionFit: When a coin is flipped, a person calls one side, often the reverse of heads.

clue.text: Dislike of others making sad man this inadequate

indicators.note: sad here means in a sorry state, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: ropy is British slang for poor or inadequate

explanation.surface: Something that makes a gloomy man feel so inadequate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sad' looks like a description but rearranges MAN THIS to MISANTH. ROPY is informal British for shoddy.
explanation.definitionFit: This is hatred or distrust of humankind in general.
